name: custom_axis
description: The default 1100x860 Custom Axes Gallery example on its Dual scale spectrum tab.

checks.expectation: The gallery title and three-tab bar appear above a description and one large spectrum plot. All content fits in the window without unintended overlap.
Dual scale is visibly selected, with Multi-rate and Shared time visible as the other tabs. The Wavelength and frequency on one spectrum heading and explanatory copy are readable.

Two distinct horizontal axes are visible below the plot: Wavelength (nm) increases from roughly 400 to 700 left-to-right, while Frequency (THz) decreases left-to-right. Their tick labels and titles do not visibly collide. If exact ordering is not readable at the screenshot resolution, report uncertain rather than fail; fail only for a clearly visible contradiction or collision.
A continuous emission spectrum with three clearly visible peaks is drawn against the Relative intensity axis, including a tallest central peak.

The plot's axis titles and tick labels are intentionally smaller, normal-weight, and light gray, while the gallery title and tab labels are larger, brighter, or bolder. Those intended typography and contrast differences are not rasterization defects, so do not use the title or tabs as a direct sharpness comparison. Fail only when the plot glyphs show concrete low-resolution artifacts such as square pixel blocks, doubled or jagged stair-step edges, or obvious uniform upscaling relative to any similarly sized and styled text. Normal antialiasing, small or low-contrast text, and differences caused by rotated text are acceptable. If the axis text remains readable and no concrete scaling artifact is visible, pass this check.
Axes, grid, tick labels, and curve are not blank, corrupted, clipped, or drawn outside their intended areas.
